entries.title: Elwynn Forest
body: Elwynn is the green heart of the kingdom of Stormwind: oak woods, quiet lakes and farmland folded between the mountains, with the white walls of Stormwind City rising at its north-western edge. Farmsteads, vineyards and logging camps are strung along the roads that meet at Goldshire.

It has not always been peaceful. When the orcish Horde first came through the Dark Portal, it burned its way north through these woods and razed Stormwind itself. The forest grew back and the city was rebuilt, but the land never quite settled. Today kobolds dig in its mines, Riverpaw gnolls prowl its southern edge, murlocs creep up its streams, and a gang of masked thieves called the Defias works the roads.
With so much of the army away on distant fronts, the forest's defence falls to a handful of marshals, their deputies, and whoever is willing to pick up a sword and help.
sources: quest 783 offer text (forces marshaled abroad, lawless groups within)
pre-Cataclysm lore: First War, sack of Stormwind

entries.title: Northshire Valley
body: A sheltered valley in the hills north of Goldshire, closed off from the rest of Elwynn by a gate on the southern road. The abbey stands at its centre, surrounded by vineyards, a stable and the farmers' wagons.

Northshire has long been a place where new defenders of the kingdom learn their trade. Lately it has needed them: kobolds have crept down from the woods to the north, the wolves of the valley are falling sick, and thieves in red bandanas have been seen across the river to the east.
sources: quest 54 description (Goldshire lies along the southern road, past the border gates)

entries.title: Northshire Abbey
body: The abbey is a house of the Holy Light, a place of prayer, healing and study whose monks also tend the valley's vines and keep its stores of food and wine. Brother Neals, who manages those stores, likes to do his tasting up in the bell tower.

Its halls double as a training ground. Priests and paladins learn their first lessons here, and Marshal McBride runs the valley's defence from inside its doors, sending each new volunteer out to deal with whatever trouble is nearest.
sources: quest 3905 description and offer text (Brother Neals, bell tower, food and drink)

entries.title: Echo Ridge Mine
body: A mine in the ridge at the valley's northern end. The kobolds who took it are not mere scavengers: they came in numbers, set up camp outside, and work the tunnels for themselves, carrying candles on their heads against the dark.
Marshal McBride's scouts first took them for a nuisance. The deeper anyone goes into Echo Ridge, the clearer it becomes that the kobolds mean to stay.

entries.title: Northshire Vineyards
body: Rows of vines in the south-east of the valley, tended by the farmer Milly Osworth. The grapes go to the abbey, where they become the brothers' wine.
The Defias moved into the vineyards in the middle of a harvest. Milly had already gathered most of her grapes into buckets, and had to leave them standing among the vines when she fled.

entries.title: Goldshire
body: The largest town in Elwynn sits where the road from Stormwind meets the road east, a cluster of timber houses around the Lion's Pride Inn, a smithy and a town square. Travellers, farmers and would-be heroes all pass through, and most of them stop for a drink.

Goldshire is also where the forest's defence is run. Marshal Dughan keeps watch from the square, taking in reports of gnolls in the west, kobolds in the mines and murlocs in the east, and trying to make too few soldiers cover all of them.
sources: quests 40, 39, 62, 76, 239 (Dughan in Goldshire, reports from every side)
quest 2158 (the Lion's Pride, road south from Stormwind)

entries.title: The Lion's Pride Inn
body: Goldshire's inn and the forest's best-known meeting place. Innkeeper Farley keeps a fire burning for the tired and the cold, and his friends in the city send newcomers his way for a bed and a meal.
Upstairs and at the back, all sorts of people take rooms. The apothecary William Pestle has been staying here while he gathers ingredients in the countryside.
sources: quest 107 (William Pestle staying at the Lion's Pride)

entries.title: Fargodeep Mine
body: A mine almost due south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure homesteads. Kobolds overran it, as they did Northshire's, and some of them carry gold dust and wax candles out of its tunnels.
Among them is a big kobold with a gold tooth who has a habit of picking up shiny things that aren't his, including, the farmers say, at least one widow's necklace.

entries.title: Jasperlode Mine
body: A mine in the foothills north of the Tower of Azora, east along the road from Goldshire. It was the farther of the forest's two troubled mines, and for a while the marshals hoped it had been spared.
It had not. Kobolds hold Jasperlode too, and with both mines lost, the gold that should flow from Elwynn's hills to the crown has found other hands to fall into.
sources: quest 123, 147 (gold from the Elwynn mines going to the Collector)

entries.title: The Stonefield and Maclure Farms
body: Two neighbouring farms south of Goldshire, the Stonefields' fields to the west and the Maclures' vineyards to the east, and between them a feud older than anyone can explain. The families don't speak, don't trade and don't trust each other's children.

The quarrels are small and endless. Auntie Bernice Stonefield is sure young Billy Maclure took her necklace. Ma Stonefield blames a prize pig from the Brackwell farm for her vegetables. And the youngest of each family are in love with each other, which helps nobody.
sources: quest 62 (mine between the Stonefield and Maclure homesteads)

entries.title: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch
body: The Brackwell farm lies east of the Maclure vineyards. Its most famous resident was a sow called Princess, a prize-winner grown enormous on her neighbours' vegetables.

The farm has fallen into worse company since. The Defias camp among its pumpkins, and a schedule taken from one of them named it as the hideout of a man known only as the Collector, who received the gold stolen from Elwynn's mines.

entries.title: Tower of Azora
body: A slender mage tower beside the eastern road, a landmark for travellers heading toward Redridge and for anyone looking for the path north to Jasperlode Mine. The mage Theocritus keeps it now.
Wizards rarely explain themselves to farmers, and the people of eastern Elwynn are content to leave the tower and its keeper alone, so long as nothing strange comes out of it.
sources: quest 76 (tower on the east road, mine to its north)

entries.title: Eastvale Logging Camp
body: Elwynn's oaks have built much of Stormwind, and much of the lumber comes from this camp in the eastern woods, beyond the bridge Guard Thomas watches. Supervisor Raelen runs the work; Sara Timberlain makes cloth and leather armour here for those who defend the forest.

Life at the camp is not easy. Wolves and bears press in from the forest, bolder every season, and workers have fled from bundles of wood they had already cut. The camp has deadlines to meet all the same.
sources: quest 52 (Eastvale suffers attacks from wolves and bears)
quest 59 (Sara Timberlain beyond Guard Thomas' post)

entries.title: Stone Cairn Lake
body: A lake in north-eastern Elwynn, north of the bridge on the east road. Murlocs have built a village of huts on its eastern shore, one of several they have raised along the streams of the forest.

Two of Stormwind's footmen, Rolf Hartford and Malakai Stone, were sent up the river to find out why. Neither came back. Their medallions were found on the shore and in the village, and with them the proof that the murlocs were more than a rumour.

entries.title: Westbrook Garrison
body: A small garrison on Elwynn's western border, just past the brook on the road to Westfall. Deputy Rainer commands it, with fewer soldiers than he needs.

The garrison watches the edge of the forest where it meets the Westfall farmlands, and the edge is restless: gnolls of the Riverpaw pack have crossed into the woods to the south, and thieves move freely along the road.
sources: quest 11 (gnolls south of the guard tower)

entries.title: Ridgepoint Tower
body: A watchtower at the forest's far eastern edge, where the road climbs out of Elwynn toward the red hills of Redridge and the town of Lakeshire.
It marks the end of the forest's gentler country. Beyond it, the kingdom's soldiers face orcs of the Blackrock clan and gnolls far more dangerous than any that trouble Goldshire.
sources: pre-Cataclysm geography of the Elwynn-Redridge border

entries.title: Marshal McBride
body: The marshal of Northshire, who commands the valley's defence from inside the abbey. He is brisk with volunteers, and he has seen a great many of them.

McBride knows how thin the kingdom's forces are stretched, and he treats the valley's kobolds, wolves and thieves as one more front in a long campaign. Those who prove themselves to him are sent south to Goldshire with papers naming them acting deputies of the Stormwind Marshals.

entries.title: Marshal Dughan
body: The marshal of Goldshire, responsible for most of Elwynn. Reports reach him from every direction: gnolls in the west, kobolds in two mines, murlocs in the east, thieves on the roads and a giant gnoll in the south-western woods.

Dughan is a careful commander with too few soldiers, and he does not move them on rumour. It took the deaths of two footmen to convince him the murlocs were a real threat. He has found more use for the adventurers who pass through town, and pays them from the army's bounties.
sources: quests 35, 39, 40 offer texts (Dughan not convinced until the military report)

entries.title: Hogger
body: A gnoll of enormous size who roams the woods of south-western Elwynn, near the Westfall border. Every attempt to capture him has failed, and the Stormwind Army has put a generous bounty on his head.

Hogger runs with the Riverpaw gnolls who have spread out of Westfall into the forest, and he is the closest thing they have to a leader there. To the soldiers of Goldshire he is a constant headache; to young adventurers he is the first real test of their courage.

entries.title: Tommy Joe and Maybell
body: Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure are young, in love, and on opposite sides of a family feud. Maybell passes letters to Tommy Joe, who waits by the river west of his family's farm, while their elders glare at each other across the fields.

Gramma Stonefield, who remembers being young, took their side, and William Pestle at the Lion's Pride brewed an invisibility liquor so Maybell could slip away unseen. Whether the families ever learn of it is another matter.

entries.title: William Pestle
body: An apothecary who runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District with his brother Morgan. William spends much of his time in Goldshire, buying what the countryside can offer: wax from kobold candles, kelp from the murlocs of Crystal Lake.
He is a kindly man with a soft spot for the young lovers of the Stonefield and Maclure farms, and he would rather solve a problem with the right potion than with a sword.

entries.title: Remy "Two Times"
body: A merchant of Goldshire known for saying everything twice. Remy buys gold dust from anyone willing to take it off the kobolds, at the best price in town, the best price in town.

Remy was among the first to warn Marshal Dughan about murlocs moving up the eastern streams. He also mentions, now and then, associates whose tokens he hands out with his payments. Nobody in Goldshire asks who they are.

entries.title: Morgan the Collector
body: A Defias thief who hid among the pumpkins of the Brackwell farm and received gold taken from Elwynn's mines on a fixed schedule, which is how the marshals learned of him.

On his finger he wore a ring of the old Stonemasons' Guild of Stormwind. Why a common thief should carry an artisan's guild ring, and why the Defias were collecting gold from the kingdom's mines, were questions Marshal Dughan could not answer.

entries.title: The Stonemasons' Debt
body: After the Second War, Stormwind City had to be raised again from its ruins. The work fell to the Stonemasons' Guild, led by a master builder named Edwin VanCleef, who rebuilt the capital stone by stone.

When the walls were finished, the city's House of Nobles refused to pay what the masons were owed. The masons rioted, and in the trouble that followed the queen was killed. The guild was driven out of the city.

Many of the masons did not scatter. Under VanCleef they became a brotherhood of thieves who call themselves the Defias, and they have spread through Elwynn and Westfall, robbing the kingdom that robbed them. The red bandanas worn by the bandits of Northshire are the sign of that old grudge.
sources: quest 147 offer text (Stonemasons' Guild ring on a Defias thief)
pre-Cataclysm lore: Stonemasons' Guild, House of Nobles, VanCleef, death of Queen Tiffin

entries.title: Murlocs in the Streams
body: In recent months murlocs have been moving up the streams of eastern Elwynn, from the rivers toward Crystal Lake and Stone Cairn Lake. They have built villages, driven off the fish and attacked anyone who comes near.

Nobody knows why they came. The guards who have fought them say they are aggressive and cleverer than they look. For a long time Goldshire treated the reports as merchants' gossip; it was only after two footmen died at Stone Cairn Lake that the Stormwind Army put a bounty on their fins.

entries.title: An Army Abroad
body: Stormwind has fought war after war for a generation, and much of its army still serves far from home. What soldiers remain are spread thinly across the kingdom's many borders.

Into that gap have come thieves, gnolls and worse, and the marshals of Elwynn have come to rely on volunteers: farmers' sons and daughters, travellers, adventurers of every race of the Alliance. They are given papers, a few coins from the army's bounties, and a long list of troubles to deal with.
sources: quest 54 offer text (Acting Deputy Status; army busy for the nobles)
